Judicial Branch testimony in favor of LD 20, An Act Regarding the First
Judicial District and the District Court Locations in the Judicial Divisions of Androscoggin and Western Aroostook:

Senator Carney, Representative Kuhn, members of the Joint Standing Committee on
Judiciary, my name is Julie Finn and I represent the Judicial Branch. LD 20 was submitted by the Judicial Branch and I am here today to testify in support of the bill.

The Judicial Branch plans to close the Madawaska District Court, which is presently open only two days per month. This change will increase the operational efficiency of the courts.

There are many reasons for this proposal which are enumerated below:

0 There is a comparatively small number of cases that are heard in Madawaska
resulting in the court opening for two days per month, one day for criminal matters and one day for civil and family matters.

0 Because the Madawaska court is only open two days per month, it cannot accept
filings, motions, or anything else delivered to the court by the US Postal Service. However, the
notices of court proceedings that occur in Madawaska list the Madawaska address because that is where litigants have to appear for court. This can create problems for court users. For example, if an individual is summonsed to the Madawaska's court address for a hearing, calls in and wishes not to contest the matter and pay the waiverable fine, and subsequently sends the fine to the address in Madawaska, this piece of mail will not be delivered and the court will not know that the fine has been paid.
